stem: The Paris Agreement (2015) aims to limit global average temperature rise to well below:

options.option_text: 2°C above pre-industrial levels, with efforts to limit to 1.5°C

subject: Environment & Ecology
explanation: Paris Agreement (COP21, December 2015): limit warming to 'well below 2°C' and pursue 1.5°C. Countries submit NDCs (Nationally Determined Contributions). India committed to 40% non-fossil electricity by 2030 and carbon intensity reduction. The 1.5°C target was reinforced at COP26 (Glasgow, 2021).

stem: The Kyoto Protocol was adopted in which year and under which convention?
subject: Environment & Ecology
explanation: Kyoto Protocol: adopted December 1997 at COP3 in Kyoto, Japan, under the UNFCCC (United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change). It came into force in 2005. It set binding emission reduction targets for developed (Annex I) countries. The UNFCCC itself was adopted at Rio Earth Summit in 1992.

stem: COP stands for in the context of climate negotiations:
subject: Environment & Ecology
explanation: COP = Conference of the Parties — the supreme decision-making body of the UNFCCC. Parties = countries that have ratified the treaty. COP meetings are held annually (e.g., COP21=Paris 2015, COP26=Glasgow 2021, COP27=Sharm el-Sheikh 2022, COP28=Dubai 2023).

stem: Which summit led to the establishment of the UNFCCC and was known as the 'Earth Summit'?
subject: Environment & Ecology
explanation: The 1992 Rio Earth Summit (UNCED — UN Conference on Environment and Development) produced the UNFCCC, CBD (Convention on Biological Diversity) and UNCCD (land degradation). Stockholm (1972) was the first global env. conference; Johannesburg (2002) was Rio+10; Copenhagen (2009) = COP15.

stem: The 'Montreal Protocol' addresses which environmental issue?
subject: Environment & Ecology
explanation: Montreal Protocol (1987): phased out production of CFCs (chlorofluorocarbons) and other ozone-depleting substances. The ozone layer in the stratosphere filters UV-B radiation. The protocol is considered the most successful multilateral environmental agreement — the ozone hole is recovering. Distinct from UNFCCC which covers greenhouse gases and climate.

stem: India's target under the Paris Agreement (NDC) includes achieving what percentage of cumulative electric power from non-fossil fuel sources by 2030?
subject: Environment & Ecology
explanation: India updated its NDC in 2022: achieve 50% cumulative electric power from non-fossil fuels by 2030 (up from the original 40% target). India also targets to reduce emission intensity of GDP by 45% from 2005 levels, and create additional carbon sink of 2.5–3 billion tonnes of CO₂ through forests.

stem: The 'Green Climate Fund' was established to:

options.option_text: Fund green infrastructure in developed nations
Help developing countries adapt to and mitigate climate change

subject: Environment & Ecology
explanation: The Green Climate Fund (GCF) was established under the UNFCCC at COP16 (Cancún, 2010). Developed nations committed to mobilising USD 100 billion/year by 2020 for developing countries to address climate change through adaptation (resilience) and mitigation (emission reduction).

stem: The Ramsar Convention (1971) relates to the conservation of:
subject: Environment & Ecology
explanation: Ramsar Convention on Wetlands (signed in Ramsar, Iran, 1971) is an intergovernmental treaty for the conservation of wetlands. India has 75+ Ramsar sites (as of 2022-23) — highest in Asia. Chilika Lake (Odisha) was India's first Ramsar site (1981). Note: distinct from the CBD (forests/biodiversity) and CMS (migratory species).

stem: The 'carbon credit' mechanism was introduced under:
subject: Environment & Ecology
explanation: The Kyoto Protocol introduced three 'flexible mechanisms': Emissions Trading (ET), Clean Development Mechanism (CDM), and Joint Implementation (JI) — all of which use carbon credits. 1 credit = right to emit 1 tonne of CO₂ equivalent. This cap-and-trade approach was a significant innovation.

stem: COP28 (2023), which reached a historic agreement to 'transition away from fossil fuels', was held in:
subject: Environment & Ecology
explanation: COP28 (Nov–Dec 2023): Dubai, UAE. First historic agreement to 'transition away from fossil fuels.' COP26 = Glasgow (2021, UK); COP27 = Sharm el-Sheikh (2022, Egypt); COP29 = Baku, Azerbaijan (2024). The host city changes each year.

stem: 'NAPCC' (National Action Plan on Climate Change) in India was launched in which year?
subject: Environment & Ecology
explanation: NAPCC was launched by Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on 30 June 2008. It has 8 National Missions: Solar Energy, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Sustaining Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture, and Strategic Knowledge for Climate Change. It is India's framework for climate action.
